purpose: Pre-registered choice of the max-age intervention threshold A, from measured baseline timing/capacity only. Written BEFORE any guarded-arm return was computed.

pre_registration.rule: A = 2 x (baseline median per-host end-of-episode investigation age), rounded to a multiple of 8 ticks. The 2x factor keeps the guard a tail intervention on the starved agent instead of a disguised strict coverage guard; the multiple of 8 keeps it a round simulator-aligned number.
pre_registration.capability_argument: A threshold the busiest agent cannot meet is not a bound, it is a starvation loop: the guard would re-pick the same oldest host every time it was consulted. The factor is chosen so that the guard binds on the tail and abstains elsewhere.

sensitivity_rationale.24: near the well-covered agents' p90 (25-34): likely to bind broadly, i.e. approach the strict guard. Reported as the over-constraining case.
sensitivity_rationale.96: near the starved agent's end-of-episode p90 (124): expected to bind rarely, i.e. approach the unguarded arm. Reported as the under-constraining case.

baseline_evidence.service_capacity: one pending action per agent; agent 4 needs 26x2 = 52 ticks for one clean sweep of its 26 hosts out of a 400-tick episode, before any rule-1 remediation or rule-2 verification decision.
baseline_evidence.coverage_design_finding: unguarded lancer coverage was already 1.000 (0 never-investigated in 32/32 seeds); the guard bought freshness, not coverage

policy_identity.claim: The repaired harness reproduces the historical heuristic arm exactly, so a difference between arms can only come from the arm.

historical_evidence_invalidated.reason: max_age is final-tick age conflated with max age during the episode and was constant 398 for the 32-seed re-runs; det_delay_median measured the tick an analysis was REQUESTED, kept only the first per host and counted failed requests; coverage used the requested-host set. n_undetected and the per-host compromise set included the 8 non-defendable contractor_network hosts.
